top_signal.title: I landed UNFI distribution and hundreds of Whole Foods stores. How do I turn that foothold into growth when operations and surprise expenses take everything I have?
top_signal.summary: I’m the founder and sole operator of a small food brand I’ve been building for 7 years. I still own 100% and strongly prefer to keep it family-owned. I’ve landed UNFI distribution and placement in several hundred Whole Foods stores coast to coast. That foothold has sustained me, but maintaining it takes so much work that over the past few years I’ve struggled to find the time and resources to grow enough to outpace costs.   Revenue has hovered around $200–350K annually for the past three to four years. There’s lots of product love and repeat business, but servicing the business consumes nearly all my time, leaving little capacity for sales outreach. Every time I start building a cash cushion, another operational problem eats through it. A few recent equipment breakdowns have made the situation urgent. My credit is exhausted, cash is effectively gone, and the operational workload hasn’t eased.   Our revenue breaks down roughly as follows:     60%: UNFI, primarily Whole Foods   15%: Other regional distributors   20%: Amazon   5%: Our website     Adding new stores and chains through distributors is harder and takes longer, but can add dozens of locations at once. Amazon and Shopify pay faster, which matters urgently, but hundreds of ad experiments and millions of content views haven’t produced a reliable way to acquire customers.
